contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-managed-payments-setup-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-setup.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/set-up`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/set-up describes Stripe's merchant-of-record solution for eligible digital products, including indirect tax compliance in more than 80 countries, fraud prevention, disputes and transaction-level support. It calls for product eligibility, Dashboard activation, a development environment, API version 2025-03-31.basil or later and an eligible tax code on the Product. Create recurring or one-time Prices through Dashboard or API (new raw lines 5-26, 34-46 and 96-148). The merchant's checkout button calls a server endpoint that creates a Checkout Session with a Price line item, mode subscription or payment, and managed_payments[enabled]=true. The server redirects to the returned Stripe-hosted URL. Explicit false disables Managed Payments for that Session (new raw lines 164-172 and 278-320). Use webhook events for downstream actions. Session completion and the browser return are distinct from a delayed payment's later success or failure (new raw lines 382-410). A Managed Payments subscription authorizes Managed Payments charges only, and an outside charge needs appropriate separate consent (new raw lines 425-437). The guide distinguishes Link's customer-facing MoR role and sandbox visibility, and applies the Price's tax behavior before the Dashboard default (new raw lines 449-470). The April 23 capture describes the same hosted flow, true flag and event separation, and explicitly requires merchant Dashboard ToS acceptance and all purchased products to be eligible (old raw lines 8-19, 308-366 and 450-464). source-stripe-managed-payments-setup.md preserves April's central flow but omits Dashboard activation and the development environment and overstates what happens to a Session with an ineligible item. It lacks the November per-Session false setting.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/set-up, the substantive November documentation addition is explicit false as a per-Checkout-Session opt-out, with no evidence that this was a new API launch, changed an existing Session or converted a subscription (old raw lines 308-360 and new raw lines 278-314). The November MoR introduction expands the April scope description and gives the dated 80-plus-country indirect-tax statement, while the new setup prerequisites omit the express Dashboard merchant ToS sentence and shorten the all-products statement to general product eligibility. Keep the April 23 claims with their original date and avoid inferring a policy relaxation, mixed-cart fallback or Session-create error from these passages (old raw lines 8-19 and new raw lines 5-16). Correct the mixed-cart overstatement in source-stripe-managed-payments-setup.md and qualify related source-route wording in the Stripe index and Managed Payments concept. The sample shifts from Node/Express to cURL and Ruby/Sinatra, reorganized steps, table copy edits and new eligibility/tax links change presentation or navigation (old raw lines 59-105, 368-432 and 528-531, new raw lines 62-94, 322-380 and 472-477). The new setup demonstrates hosted Checkout (new raw lines 164-172 and 278-320). The November 7 update-checkout capture names an existing hosted or embedded payment- or subscription-mode Session integration at lines 9-18, while its lines 74-100 show hosted success_url examples. Qualify the Managed Payments concept's broad restriction at line 83 by distinguishing embedded_page from the Checkout Elements UI and without extrapolating hosted examples to embedded. The November Sessions Create reference lines 198-199, 464-477 and 512-525 distinguishes hosted success_url and optional cancel_url from the conditionally required return_url for embedded_page or elements. This also resolves the setup prose that assigns both hosted destinations to success_url (old raw lines 338-360 and new raw lines 278-314). Date-qualify the API floor of 2025-03-31.basil or later and all-products eligibility shorthand at Managed Payments concept line 120, Checkout concept line 286 and Stripe index line 135. The November 7 how-it-works capture lines 25-36 explicitly excludes custom domains from Managed Payments checkouts, an exception to the generic hosted feature at Checkout concept lines 129-133. Keep the version floor, server creation/client redirect, three webhook events, subscription charge consent, Link sandbox behavior and Price tax default conditional on an unspecified tax behavior. A 303, a browser return or checkout.session.completed alone gives no proof of success for a delayed payment, settlement or eligibility (old raw lines 434-526 and new raw lines 382-470).
